title: prioritize runbook quicklinks and enhance SLO Toolkit autodiagnostics
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: on-call engineers rely on the incident-bot quicklinks card to surface runbooks and suggested actions during paging. In high-noise situations the card surfaced too many irrelevant links and under-prioritized runbooks that covered high-SLO-impact services. This PR introduces a prioritized quicklinks ranking for runbooks and tightens SLO Toolkit autodiagnostics scoring so suggestions better reflect impact and recent on-call feedback.

What changed: added a runbook ranking pipeline that combines SLO impact, last-runbook-invocation recency, oncall-feedback score, and operational play priority. Tied the pipeline into incident-bot quicklinks generation and the SLO Toolkit autodiagnostics scorer. Added feature flag (ONCALL_QUICKLINK_RANKING) and knobbed defaults to be conservative (rollout via feature flag).

Key user-visible behavior: quicklinks shown on Slack/Console will now be ordered by a priority score; top-3 links are pinned. Autodiagnostics suggestions are re-ranked to prefer runbooks that historically resolved incidents for the same SLO group. New telemetry emitted for quicklink clicks, suggestion acceptance, and rank drift.

Implementation notes: incremental rollout – feature flag gated, existing tests updated, new unit tests cover ranking edge cases, new integration test simulates a high-noise alert burst. Performance: ranking is CPU-bound but memoized per-alert for 60s to avoid repeated computation; added a lightweight cache with TTL.

Rollout plan: enable feature flag for internal oncall team for 72h, monitor quicklink CTR and suggestion acceptance; rollback flag if CTR drops >15% or error rate increases.

Related: ENG-3421 (runbook discovery improvements), SRE-177 (oncall friction reduction)
